name: Opus Momentum
strategy: Cross-sectional price momentum ranked on 12-1 and 6-month returns: long energy E&P (XOP), healthcare and biotech (XLV, IBB), cybersecurity (CIBR) and a further-trimmed semiconductor sleeve (SMH), against the persistent losers: uranium miners (URA), China internet (KWEB), homebuilders (ITB) and long-duration Treasuries (TLT).
reassessment_note: Re-ranked on Yahoo daily closes through 2026-10-30. Semis have rolled over: SMH -15.4% over 1m with 6m only +2.5% (12-1 still +70%), NVDA 6m +3.1% and 12-1 +14% now below the leader cohort; I could not find a dated news cause, so this is a tape-driven trim, not a narrative one. NVDA exits, SMH is cut 18->10. Healthcare/biotech has become the second-strongest group (XLV 6m +27%, IBB 6m +30%/12-1 +29%), so XLV goes 12->14 and IBB is added at 8. On the short side URA (6m -40%, 12-1 -28%) is now the weakest liquid loser and is added at 6; KWEB (-39% 12-1, -21% 6m) goes up 6->8; ITB's loser signal is fading (6m only -2%, +6% 1m) so it is cut 12->6. The Fed held at 3.75-4% on 10-28 with two hike dissents and a December hike priced, which keeps the TLT short valid at 6. With the 11-03 midterms right after entry, net long stays a moderate 34% and cash rises to 14%.

positions.thesis: Top-ranked on both horizons (12-1 +45%, 6m +15%, 1m +10.6%) with crude (USO 12-1 +107%) still trending. It stays the largest leg at an unchanged 20%, and the existing 12% stop is kept.
Healthcare momentum is accelerating: 6m +27%, 3m +14%, 1m +11%, 12-1 +15%. The leg is +3.1% since 10-26. Raised 12->14 as the defensive momentum leader in a hawkish-Fed tape.

New entrant. Biotech qualifies on both horizons (12-1 +29%, 6m +30%, 3m +17%), one of only a few groups strong on every lookback. Sized at 8% because it overlaps XLV in sector, and it adds smid-cap biotech dispersion that XLV's megacap pharma does not carry.

Still the strongest 6m ranker in the universe at +47%, with 12-1 at +34%. The leg is down 6.8% since 10-26 as tech sold off, which is noise against that signal. Held at 8%, and the 12% stop (about 95.4) is kept to cap it.

12-1 is still +70%, so the blended rank keeps it in the long book, but 6m has collapsed to +2.5% and 1m is -15%. Cut 18->10 so a breaking trend cannot dominate the book. The stop is reset against the new fill.

New short. It is the weakest liquid loser in the ranked universe: 6m -40%, 12-1 -28%, 3m -17%, 1m -15%, consistent on every horizon. Sized at 6% with a 12% stop because a thematic ETF like this can squeeze on policy headlines.
A persistent loser on every horizon (12-1 -39%, 6m -21%, 3m -21%, 1m -6.5%), and the leg is +2% since 10-26. Raised 6->8 as the highest-conviction short.

12-1 is still -13%, but 6m has faded to -2% and it is +6% on the month, so the loser signal is weakening. The leg is -3.2%. Cut 12->6 and kept only because a December hike priced in keeps mortgage rates as a headwind.

A long-duration loser (12-1 -14%, 6m -4%). The 10-28 FOMC held at 3.75-4% with two votes to hike and a December hike priced. Its +5% 1m bounce argues against adding, so it stays at 6% with a tight 8% stop.
